subject: Post-call recap: MedX privacy & on-prem constraints — recap & checklist
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Amina Qureshi <amina.qureshi@medxhealth.com>, Gabe Thompson <gabe.thompson@medxhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: MedX privacy & on-prem constraints — recap & checklist

Hi Amina / Gabe —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have a shared checklist and clear next steps for the Private (VPC / on-prem) deployment discussion:

Summary of requirements we captured:
- PII scope: patient names, MRNs, limited PHI fields (diagnosis codes, encounter dates).
- Retention: short-term inference logs (30–90 days, needs confirmation), long-term audit logs (legal hold/audit: up to 7 years).
- Strict egress: no public internet access from model hosts; all outbound must go through customer-managed endpoints (VPC endpoints or approved NAT with allowlist).
- Air-gap possibility: customer may require an air-gapped install where the runtime has zero outbound connections — model artifacts delivered via appliance or pre-staged transfer.
- KMS: customer-managed keys required for at-rest encryption; HSM integration preferred for keys used in inference logging.
- KV cache persistence: preference for ephemeral in-memory only; no disk persistence unless encrypted and customer-approved.

Attachments included: network-diagram.png (proposed topology), medx-psa-draft.pdf (PSA / initial SOW).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Amina / Gabe: confirm the exact PII fields and the required retention windows for inference vs audit logs.
2) Security: confirm whether a full air-gap is required or if a VPC-only deployment (no public egress) is acceptable.
3) Provide allowed CIDR blocks and any approved outbound domains (e.g., S3 endpoints, KMS endpoints).
4) We'll prepare a short technical runbook and an egress allowlist checklist for your infra team — see attached draft checklist.

Plan: if you confirm the above, we propose a focused technical workshop with our infra/security engineer (Karthik) next week to map the network flows and finalize the transfer process for model artifacts.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmations.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

- medx-psa-draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

From: Amina Qureshi <amina.qureshi@medxhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Gabe Thompson <gabe.thompson@medxhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: MedX privacy & on-prem constraints — recap & checklist

Thanks Vanessa — good summary. A few clarifications from the security team after reviewing notes: 

Confirmed / clarifications:
- PII fields: names, MRNs, DOB, limited note excerpts. No full PHI dumps are permitted to leave our controlled environment.
- Retention: inference logs (redwood runtime request+response metadata) — 30 days default; audit logs (access + system logs) — 7 years for compliance. We'll confirm final numbers by next Wednesday.
- Egress: public internet egress from model hosts is not permitted. All outbound traffic must be to pre-approved VPC endpoints or through a customer-managed NAT gateway with strict allowlist.
- Air-gap: we prefer a VPC-only deployment with no public egress as the first option. An air-gapped appliance is a possibility but will require additional procurement paperwork and is a second-choice due to ops overhead.
- KV cache: must default to in-memory only; if persisted to disk, it must be encrypted with customer KMS and we need controls to purge regularly.

Questions for Redwood (please have Karthik weigh in):
1) Can Redwood support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS or HSM) for both model artifacts at rest and for encrypting runtime logs?
2) If we go VPC-only, what minimal set of outbound domains/IPs does Redwood need (list of endpoints for KMS, metrics ingress, license check, model telemetry if any)?
3) For air-gap installs: what are the recommended transfer methods for initial model artifacts (SCP to an appliance, signed portable images, or ship an encrypted drive)?

I've attached the latest security questionnaire (MedX_security_questionnaire_v2.docx) with marked fields we need answered. We'll aim to get the CIDR blocks and stricter retention numbers to you by 2026-07-14.

Thanks — Amina
Amina Qureshi
Director, Security & Privacy | MedX Health
amina.qureshi@medxhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

Attachment: MedX_security_questionnaire_v2.docx (DOCX, 85KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Amina Qureshi <amina.qureshi@medxhealth.com>, Gabe Thompson <gabe.thompson@medxhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: MedX privacy & on-prem constraints — recap & checklist

Amina / team — thanks for the clear guidance. Adding technical detail and options below so we can converge quickly: 

KMS / keys:
- Redwood supports Customer-Managed Keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS and can integrate with external HSMs for on-prem HSM-backed keys. We can encrypt model artifacts, runtime caches (if persisted), and logs using CMKs.

Egress / endpoints (VPC-only deployment):
- Minimal required outbound endpoints (if you permit any egress):
  * kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (or your regional KMS endpoint)
  * s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (S3 via VPC endpoint recommended; disable public S3 access)
  * registry.redwood-inference.com (for license and model manifest checks) — can be allowlisted to specific IPs
  * metrics.redwood-inference.com (optional; can be disabled for on-prem installs)
- If you require no outbound connectivity, we can disable remote telemetry/license checks and perform offline license verification via signed manifests.

Model artifacts transfer / air-gap options:
1) Pre-staged artifacts via secure staging S3 with a temporary presigned URL delivered over a SFTP channel that terminates inside your environment.
2) Encrypted portable images (signed) shipped on removable media and ingested by our private installer.
3) Direct SCP from an approved Redwood host into a customer-controlled gateway during a scheduled maintenance window.

KV cache and persistence:
- Default runtime can be configured to keep KV cache strictly in-memory and never persist to disk.
- If persistent caching is required for performance, it will be encrypted using CMK and we can provide purge APIs and an agreed retention TTL.

Logs and retention:
- Runtime access logs and inference metadata can be configured to retain for 30 days by default; audit logs stored separately and can be configured to longer retention (7 years) and exported to your secure S3 audit bucket via VPC endpoint.

Action items (recommended):
- Amina: provide the CIDR blocks and confirm whether KMS endpoints are customer-managed inside your account (yes/no).
- Vanessa + Monica: we'll prepare a 60-minute technical workshop slide set and a downloadable checklist (redwood-private-egress-checklist.md) describing each network and KMS configuration option.

I'll be available for the workshop next week; please propose 2 windows.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-private-egress-checklist.md (MD, 7KB)
